findings.claim: The new Fast project plan does not establish teach-before-apply within the frozen Fast-day schedule. It says the 10-minute Skim teaches the day’s topic pages before the 70-minute project increment, but the same intake budgets those pages at 70 minutes on FT16 and FT17, 40 minutes on FT18, and 30 minutes on FT20. A 15-minute try-first diagnostic checks knowledge; it does not supply the missing instruction. The project therefore applies same-day objectives that the stated blocks cannot teach first.
findings.recommendation: Before authoring the project, provide a calendar-valid Fast pathway that identifies exactly which prerequisite instruction occurs before each increment and fits the fixed 120-minute template without compressing honest page budgets. Reduce an increment to already-taught objectives, or record an approved overlay scheduling mechanism; do not treat a diagnostic or an acknowledged pacing gap as teaching.

findings.claim: The S33 project-row brief is not yet aligned to all of its Project-day learning. Step 3 applies create/edit/delete and submission-error objectives from S33 only as in-build references rather than after teaching, while the plan separately says Standard learners write UI tests in step 3 but omits UI testing from step 3’s outcomes and Applies topics column. The project brief therefore neither demonstrates teach-before-apply nor states an observable UI-testing outcome for the S33 row.
findings.recommendation: Define a fixed S33 sequence that teaches/checks each S33 concept before its first project use, then add the UI-testing objective, learner action, and public-test evidence to step 3 (or explicitly move it to an authorized later Standard activity). Keep the frozen topic order and do not rely on just-in-time project references as the only teaching event.

findings.claim: The single-starter plan does not explain how both entry paths receive a usable scaffold. Fast learners begin at step 1 and extend their own work, while Standard S33 learners must begin from a provided step-2 state; one mutable starter/ described as “extended per step” cannot simultaneously represent both starting states, and no checkpoint-selection or safe handoff mechanism is specified.
findings.recommendation: Specify the scaffold/checkpoint layout and learner handoff for each project-row entry point, including which bytes Standard S33 receives, which tests are active at each step, and how later-entry scaffolding avoids committing reference solutions to earlier work. Verify each supported entry path with the one public test command.
